rationale: This is essentially a SUMRANK blend of two already-tested archive signals ("Working Capital Crowds Out Innovation" and "Tangible Expansion Crowds Out Innovation") with the identical R&D-decline leg and profitability gate, so it is a cosmetic averaging of known results rather than a new mechanism and will most likely just interpolate their existing t-stats.

The swap of a realized gross-profit-decline leg for the previously tested cash-depletion leg is a defensible payoff-validation refinement of the capacity-substitution family, though it overlaps heavily with both "Distressed Working-Capital Substitution" and the gen-0 "Profitable Inventory Divergence" and mildly double-counts gross profitability as both gate and leg.

The triple intersection of inventory build, capacity contraction, and R&D retrenchment is a genuinely untested combination whose legs are individually supported, but it is highly derivative of two neighboring archive entries and risks being driven mainly by the R&D leg rather than the substitution story.

Adding a profitability-trend deterioration leg is a substantive (not cosmetic) attempt to fix the weak cross-sectional evidence of "Capex Without Capacity Formation," though conditioning on persistently above-industry profitability while simultaneously requiring a falling profitability trend narrows the sample toward an internally tense subset and the capex-TS_RANK family has consistently produced weak fmb t-stats.

Pairing sub-depreciation physical investment with R&D contraction is the most genuinely new leg combination here and tests a coherent "broad capital starvation" mechanism, with the main caveat that archive evidence suggests the undermaintenance leg alone may carry most of the predictive power and coverage will be thin (~0.08) due to the ppent denominator.

Like the first proposal, this merely SUMRANK-averages the visible-investment legs of two already-evaluated signals ("Buy-Versus-Build Innovation Substitution" and "Tangible Expansion Crowds Out Innovation") while retaining the same R&D leg and gate, making it a rediscovery-by-blending with little incremental economic content.
